title: Test tiers and git/CI gates
summary: Verification tiers, strict test config, one dispatcher per git hook with content, message and leak checks, and optional hosted CI templates.
why: Gates that read the staged bytes and the pushed range catch what would otherwise reach history; one dispatcher per hook keeps modules from fighting over hook files, and the armed check proves the hooks really fire.

items.title: Verification tiers by change size
items.does: Adds a rule that sets how much to verify by the size of a change: compile only for cosmetic edits, the module's tests for one module, and the whole suite once, by the merger, for shared code.
items.why: When every agent runs the whole suite for every edit, the machine and the suite queue starve; most edits need far less, and shared changes still get the full run once.

items.title: Strict test runner config
items.does: Creates a pytest.ini that makes unknown markers and config keys errors, lists every skip, makes expected failures strict, keeps discovery in tests/ and keeps temp dirs only for failed runs.
items.why: A typo in a marker silently deselects tests and unnamed skips hide coverage gaps; strict settings turn both into visible errors. Python projects only; other runners keep their own config.

items.title: Impact-based test selection for push and CI
items.does: Adds a selector that prints FULL, NONE or a list of tests from the files changed since a base ref, using rules in a small text file, and escalates to the full suite on config changes or unmatched paths.
items.why: Running the full suite on every push makes the gate the bottleneck once the suite takes minutes; a selection that escalates whenever in doubt saves time without skipping affected tests.
items.notes: Enable later: when the whole suite takes several minutes and most pushes touch one area.

items.title: git pre-commit content gate
items.does: Adds a pre-commit check that reads the staged bytes and refuses non-ASCII or CR bytes in added lines, secret-shaped strings, Python that does not compile, JSON that does not parse, and files over their size budget (warning at 90 percent).
items.why: A stray typographic dash broke a PowerShell 5.1 script, and gates that read the working tree passed what was actually staged; checking the index judges exactly what gets committed.

items.title: commit-msg format checks
items.does: Adds a commit-msg check: a non-empty subject of at most 72 characters, ASCII only, no control bytes, and no placeholder subject such as wip or update.
items.why: A glyph in a commit subject went through because the glyph check ran only in pre-commit; the message needs its own check, and a placeholder subject tells the next reader nothing.
items.notes: Runs after the attribution strip: the commit-msg dispatcher runs its checks in name order.

items.title: pre-push test gate over the pushed range
items.does: Adds a pre-push check that runs the configured suite command (through the suite gate when set), refuses a run with zero tests, and refuses when HEAD moved while the suite ran.
items.why: A pre-push check once graded one commit while a later one reached the remote, and a run with zero tests read as a pass; the gate must test exactly what is pushed and must have tested something.
items.notes: Enable later: when the remote is shared and a red push would block other people.

items.title: pre-push leak scan (credentials, names, paths)
items.does: Adds a pre-push check that scans every commit in the pushed range for secret-shaped strings, home-folder paths and your own private needles, kept in a local file under .git/info that is never tracked.
items.why: Real tokens, account paths and private names have reached public history before, and removing them meant rewriting history; a scan of the whole pushed range stops them before they leave the machine.

items.title: pre-merge-commit runs the pre-commit gate
items.does: Adds a pre-merge-commit check that runs the same pre-commit checks for merge commits.
items.why: Git skips pre-commit when it creates a merge commit, so a merge once landed a non-ASCII byte on the main branch with every gate installed.

items.title: Hook installer + SessionStart armed check
items.does: Installs one dispatcher per git hook in the tracked .githooks folder, points core.hooksPath at it, and adds a check that warns once at session start when hooks are not armed; with --check it proves the pre-commit gate refuses a planted byte.
items.why: A fresh clone runs no hooks at all, and a hooks path that drifted to an absolute or moved path silently turned every gate off; one dispatcher per hook also stops modules from writing competing hook files.
items.notes: Other modules add their git checks as numbered files in .githooks/<hook>.d/ rather than writing the hook file.

items.title: PostToolUse edit guard (compile, ASCII, LF)
items.does: Adds a PostToolUse hook that checks each file Claude edits or writes: ASCII only, LF only, Python compiles, JSON parses; silent when clean, one line back to Claude when not.
items.why: A problem caught right after the edit costs one turn to fix; the same problem caught at commit time costs a re-plan, and caught later it costs a red build.

items.title: Hosted CI workflow template
items.does: Creates a GitHub Actions workflow that runs on every push, pull request and nightly: ASCII sweep, hooks-armed proof, attribution-trailer sweep and the suite, with a read-only token, full history and step timeouts below the job timeout.
items.why: Local gates can be skipped or misconfigured on one machine; CI is the shared reading every collaborator sees, and the timeouts and full history stop it from passing by doing nothing.
items.notes: Enable later: when the repo has a hosted GitHub remote; the wizard offers it when it detects one.

items.title: Docs-only push complement workflow
items.does: Creates a second workflow that runs only the tests that read docs, for repos whose main workflow ignores documentation paths.
items.why: A docs-only push once broke a size guard with no CI run at all, because the main workflow ignored docs; the complement keeps that saving without leaving docs untested.
items.notes: Enable later: when the main workflow skips docs-only pushes to save CI minutes and some tests read docs.

items.title: Main workflow runs on every push (no paths-ignore)
items.does: Adds a rule that the main workflow keeps no paths-ignore, so docs-only pushes run the whole workflow.
items.why: It is the simpler of the two ways to keep docs-only pushes tested: no second workflow to keep in step, at the cost of some CI minutes.
items.notes: Enable later: together with the hosted CI workflow; pick this or the docs complement, not both.

items.title: CodeQL weekly scan
items.does: Creates a code-scanning workflow that runs weekly and on pushes to the default branch.
items.why: It gives static security findings without a human reviewer, on a schedule, so new classes of bug show up even in weeks with no review.
items.notes: Enable later: for a public repo, or a private one with code scanning, once hosted CI is on.

items.title: Local CI script defines green
items.does: Creates ci/local-ci.sh, which runs a fixed roster of gates (ASCII sweep, compile sweep, hooks armed, the suite) and prints how many are green; a gate that checked nothing fails.
items.why: Without hosted CI, one script is the shared definition of green, and a gate that ran nothing once inherited the previous pass; a fixed roster and a fail-on-empty rule prevent both.
items.notes: Enable later: for a repo without hosted CI that still wants one written definition of green.

items.title: Gate verdict cache keyed by inputs
items.does: Adds a small cache that records a gate PASS under a hash of the commit range and the gate files, so the same range pushed to several remotes runs the gates once.
items.why: Pushing one range to four remotes once ran two dozen gate processes for the same answer; keying the cache on every input means a changed gate or range always runs again.
items.notes: Enable later: when you push the same commits to several remotes and the gates run once per remote.

items.title: Toolchain pin check
items.does: Adds tools/verify_env.py and a toolchain.txt that lists the expected interpreter, test runner and tool versions; the check runs before a suite and fails on a mismatch.
items.why: Test counts measured under a different interpreter or virtual environment were reported as if they were the real ones; checking versions first makes such counts impossible to mistake.
items.notes: Enable later: when test counts differ between machines or virtual environments.
